text: A small toy starts moving from the position of rest under a constant acceleration. If it travels a distance of 10m in t s, the distance travelled by the toy in the next t s will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A small toy begins to move from a standstill with a constant acceleration. It covers a distance of 10 meters in t seconds. We need to determine the distance the toy will travel in the subsequent t seconds.

First, we know that the initial distance traveled is given by the formula for constant acceleration starting from rest:

$\frac{1}{2}at^{2}=10\text{m}$

Next, we calculate the total distance traveled after 2t seconds:

$\frac{1}{2}a(2t)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}a\cdot 4t^{2}=2at^{2}$

Since we know from the initial condition that $\frac{1}{2}at^{2}=10\text{m}$, multiplying it by 4 gives

$2at^{2}=40\text{m}$

Thus, the additional distance traveled in the next t seconds is:

$\text{Total distance after 2t seconds}-\text{Distance already traveled in t seconds}$

$=40\text{m}-10\text{m}$

$=30\text{m}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: A person can throw a ball upto a maximum range of 100 m. How high above the ground he can throw the same ball?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine how high a person can throw a ball given the maximum range, we need to use the principles of projectile motion in physics. The maximum range of a projectile is given by the formula:

$R=\frac{v_{0}^{2}\sin (2θ)}{g}$

where:

$R$ is the range

$v_{0}$ is the initial velocity

$θ$ is the angle of projection

$g$ is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately $9.8\text{m/s}^{2}$)

The maximum range is achieved when $θ=45^{\circ }$, thus $\sin (2θ)=\sin (90^{\circ })=1$.

Given that the maximum range $R=100\text{m}$, we can rewrite the range formula as:

$100=\frac{v_{0}^{2}\cdot 1}{9.8}$

Solving for $v_{0}^{2}$:

$v_{0}^{2}=100\times 9.8=980$

Next, the maximum height $H$ reached by the ball can be calculated using the vertical component of the velocity. The formula for the maximum height is:

$H=\frac{v_{0}^{2}\sin ^{2}(θ)}{2g}$

Here, for a vertical throw, $θ=90^{\circ }$, and thus $\sin (90^{\circ })=1$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$H=\frac{v_{0}^{2}\cdot 1}{2\cdot 9.8}$

Using $v_{0}^{2}=980$, we have:

$H=\frac{980}{2\times 9.8}=\frac{980}{19.6}=50\text{m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option B: 50 m
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: The Vernier constant of Vernier callipers is 0.1 mm and it has zero error of ($-$0.05) cm. While measuring diameter of a sphere, the main scale reading is 1.7 cm and coinciding vernier division is 5. The corrected diameter will be $_________$ $\times$ $10^{-2} cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The vernier constant (least count) is $0.1\text{mm}=0.01\text{cm}$.

Observed reading $=\text{MSR}+(\text{coinciding division})\times \text{LC}=1.7\text{cm}+5\times 0.01\text{cm}=1.75\text{cm}$.

The zero error is $-0.05\text{cm}$, and the true diameter is the observed reading minus the zero error:

$d=1.75\text{cm}-(-0.05\text{cm})=1.80\text{cm}=180\times 10^{-2}\text{cm}$

Hence, the answer is 180.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of 20.0 cm for a tuning fork of frequency 400 Hz is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is $336 ms^{-1}$. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of $_____________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Wavelength of the sound: $λ=\dfrac{v}{f}=\dfrac{336}{400}=0.84\text{m}=84\text{cm}$.

A resonance tube is closed at one end, so resonances occur when the air column plus end correction $e$ equals $\dfrac{λ}{4},\dfrac{3λ}{4},\dfrac{5λ}{4},\ldots$

First resonance: $L_{1}+e=\dfrac{λ}{4}=21\text{cm}$; with $L_{1}=20.0\text{cm}$, the end correction is $e=1\text{cm}$.

Third resonance: $L_{3}+e=\dfrac{5λ}{4}=105\text{cm}\Rightarrow L_{3}=105-1=104\text{cm}$.

Hence, the answer is 104.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th June Evening Shift

text: An inductor of 0.5 mH, a capacitor of 200 $μ$F and a resistor of 2 $\Omega$ are connected in series with a 220 V ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the frequency of ac source will be $____________$ $\times$ $10^{2} Hz$.
